content.intro: Use this lesson on introduction to qunit as a professional review habit: identify the relevant behavior, make one controlled change, and verify its outcome.
content.why_it_matters: This topic is useful because it turns what qunit is into a repeatable implementation choice. Debug through reproducible steps, browser tools, focused assertions, and regression tests. QUnit can test DOM behavior and asynchronous results without assuming that a single passing unit test proves the whole application.

items: Running tests in a browser or supported test environment

content_blocks.expected_output: QUnit reports a passing assertion if the status text is updated to Ready. Load QUnit only in the test harness.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Use a local HTML page with jQuery 4.0.0 loaded before app.js for JavaScript snippets. HTML and package-manager snippets can be checked as configuration examples. Run the interaction in browser DevTools, inspect the DOM/Network panel, and compare actual behavior with the expected result. Do not submit learner code to the production API for arbitrary execution.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original markup and code, clear console/network filters, reload the local page, and repeat the same interaction. For a request example, return the mock endpoint to its original response before retrying.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with a known DOM structure, apply the pattern for introduction to qunit, and test one normal case plus one edge case. Keep selectors scoped to the intended component and verify the real browser result.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Write a focused verification case for introduction to qunit. Include a success path and a failure or edge case; record what the test does not cover.

task_acceptance_criteria: The implementation demonstrates introduction to qunit using a current, documented approach.
The learner records the expected and actual behavior and checks at least one edge case.
The example preserves semantic HTML and does not render untrusted data as HTML.
The test setup and any runtime limitation are documented honestly.
hints: First identify which DOM nodes and runtime state are involved in introduction to qunit.
Make one small change, inspect the resulting element or request, and compare it with the expected result.
If the result differs, check the selector, script order, browser console, event target, and relevant API documentation before adding more code.
content.expected_output: QUnit reports a passing assertion if the status text is updated to Ready. Load QUnit only in the test harness.
common_mistakes: Assuming a selector matched an element without checking the collection length.
Confusing jQuery collections with native DOM elements or live properties with markup attributes.
Using .html() with untrusted data or assuming client-side validation enforces server rules.
Treating a demo snippet as production-ready without testing failure and accessibility states.
summary: Introduction to QUnit is one part of the debugging, testing, and quality assurance workflow.

Debug through reproducible steps, browser tools, focused assertions, and regression tests. QUnit can test DOM behavior and asynchronous results without assuming that a single passing unit test proves the whole application.
Use the official API or upgrade guide for version-specific behavior and verify an example locally before relying on it.
